clue.text: A flaring end? So it turns out!

definitions.text: A flaring end? So it turns out!

indicators.note: something that turns out a certain way is rearranged, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses at a fiery finish and is proved right.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of 'A flaring end', rearranged as 'turns out' signals, describe a showy finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand finale is the spectacular closing number of a show, often a blaze of fireworks.

clue.text: Just nonsense having a list

parts.note: rot is plain nonsense, nothing but rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a schedule as a load of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a roster, the list saying who does which duty when.

clue.text: Standard raised on royal masthead

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word on is read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for royal (as in RN, Royal Navy)
the head of the word mast is its first letter, M

explanation.surface: A royal standard is hoisted up a flagpole.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual level or benchmark everyone is measured against.

clue.text: The leader upset her, wearing mink

indicators.note: the fur pelt is worn around the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: mink is a type of fur

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the three letters of her are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boss is annoyed with a woman dressed in her mink coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the leader's mood; it is the scramble signal, and 'wearing' says the mink coat goes round the jumbled pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Führer is German for leader, the title Hitler took.

clue.text: Sharing interest with 22 across

parts.note: 22 across is the miser of A Christmas Carol, whose interest is money; someone who shares an interest in coins is a coin collector or student of currency

explanation.surface: Two people have a hobby in common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' also suggests the interest on money, the miser's obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: A numismatologist studies coins and medals, sharing the miser's fascination with money.

clue.text: Student irene damaged a rib, in vaulting

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A student called Irene breaks a rib while doing gymnastic vaulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaulting' suggests gymnastics; it means the arched stone roof of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gothic architecture a lierne is a short connecting rib in a ribbed vault.

clue.text: I don't desire to go up the creek, but have lost my bearings

definitions.text: I don't desire to go up the creek, but have lost my bearings

parts.words: I don't desire to go up the creek, but have lost my bearings
parts.note: read as dis- plus oriented, someone not set towards the Orient (the East) has no wish to head eastward; in the plain sense, someone who has lost their bearings is confused about direction

explanation.surface: A lost boater refuses to paddle further upstream.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disoriented means being confused about where you are, lacking a sense of direction.

clue.text: Let saucepan boil over, to be concise

indicators.note: contents that boil over are thrown about, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook lets the pan bubble over.
explanation.definitionFit: To encapsulate is to sum something up briefly, putting it in a nutshell.

clue.text: The beast returns -nothing in itself

indicators.note: returns means the whole construction is read backwards
the round letter for nothing goes inside the other word

parts.note: itself refers back to nothing, so it stands for nil
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A creature comes back, though emptiness lies within it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing in itself' puts O (nothing) inside NIL (also nothing) to make NOIL, and 'returns' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is the big cat called king of the beasts.

clue.text: Old court needs stiffening with matured resin

parts.note: starch is used for stiffening collars and linen
amber is fossilised tree resin, hardened over ages

explanation.surface: An old courtroom needs firming up with aged varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star Chamber was an English court of the Tudor and Stuart era, abolished in 1641.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was a historic English law court known for secret, arbitrary hearings.

clue.text: First person to back a little bit

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the word to is reversed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The first person to support something gives only a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is the smallest Greek letter, so a tiny amount.

clue.text: Putting furniture around the grounds is a capital offence

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining an adjective: an act that is a capital offence

indicators.note: the furniture word is placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a table is an item of furniture
the grounds for something are its reason

explanation.surface: Someone moving furniture about the garden is accused of a hanging crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' suggests a garden or estate; here it means a basis or reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason against the Crown was punishable by death, the classic capital crime.

clue.text: Understood how values rose

definitions.meaning: assets that went up in worth are said to have increased in value

explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate is both to grasp something and, of an asset, to rise in worth.

clue.text: Tins are out of order for wine

indicators.note: letters out of order are no longer in their proper sequence, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wine cans have been stacked in the wrong sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Where to find holidaymakers and military types

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
sorts are kinds or types

explanation.surface: Tourists and soldiers are both to be found somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints REPORTS, but holidaymakers are found at RESORTS, which RE plus SORTS builds.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorts are holiday towns where tourists stay.

clue.text: Note ladies only turn up bearing a flower

indicators.note: in a down entry turn up reads the pieces from the bottom upwards

parts.note: E is a musical note
a ladies-only place has no men

explanation.surface: Women arrive carrying a single bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses E + NO MEN to NEMONE, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone, or windflower, is a garden plant with bright cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Used for thrusting action by troops on the jetty

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, British army gunners
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: Soldiers go into action on the jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender sword made for thrusting rather than cutting.

clue.text: In Mid-west, vine hybrid turns green?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit within the middle of west
the middle of west is its central letters
a hybrid is a mixture, so the letters of vine are mixed

explanation.surface: A crossbred grape in the American Midwest takes on a new colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mid-' takes ES from WEST and 'hybrid' makes NVIE from VINE, which goes 'In' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is called the green-eyed monster, so one who envies figuratively goes green.

clue.text: Tip Maita, in error, for the landing-place

annotationWithheld.why: Tip Maita, in error, for the landing-place: even read as Malta, the anagram needs all of TIP MALTA IN ERROR as fodder, so 'in error' would be both fodder and indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Tip Maita, in error, for the landing-place

clue.text: Coyote loose in this wem-an's cell

indicators.note: letters let loose run free and come back in another order

explanation.surface: A wild dog roams free in a woman's prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' suggests a prison; it is a biological cell, which only a woman produces.
explanation.definitionFit: An oocyte is an immature egg cell in the ovary.

clue.text: Alice gets the recipe out, to make it?

definitions.text: Alice gets the recipe out, to make it?

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the old abbreviation for recipe, as in a prescription

explanation.surface: Alice takes out a recipe to bake a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: with the recipe out, Alice can make the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a finger of choux pastry, cream-filled and chocolate-topped.

clue.text: Wearing very little — but to do so creates interest

parts.note: dressed in something
a vest is a scanty garment, so wearing very little

explanation.surface: Someone barely clad attracts attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' in the surface is attention; in the definition it is money paid on capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting money into stocks or savings earns a return.

clue.text: No point to an italian title — disregard it

indicators.note: no means the compass letter is taken away

parts.note: signore is the Italian equivalent of Mr
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman's title is pointless and should be ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something is to overlook it deliberately.

clue.text: Mean chap to score, somehow, then retreat inside

indicators.note: the retreat letters are placed inside the scrambled word
somehow means in some way, so the letters of score are reordered

parts.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word go read backwards

explanation.surface: A stingy fellow aims to win a point, then backs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to score' reads as winning a point; 'somehow' scrambles it, and 'retreat' is taken as go backwards, set 'inside' the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, Dickens's miser, gives his name to any stingy person.

clue.text: Some jam just open?

definitions.meaning: a container of preserve, a quantity of it

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a pot of preserve; as one it means slightly open, like a door.

clue.text: Chin-wag for a short space

indicators.note: to wag is to move back and forth, so the letters are shaken about

explanation.surface: A chat fills a brief gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small unit of length, a short distance.

clue.text: Born in a wood, raised here in Africa

indicators.note: the born letter goes inside the reversed wood
in a down entry raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: oak is a wood
N stands for born, from Latin natus

explanation.surface: Someone born in a forest was brought up in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Kano is a large city in northern Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Kano is a major city in northern Nigeria, so a place in Africa.

clue.text: American processing North African oil

indicators.note: processing works raw material into new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American refines oil from North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian comes from California, a US state.

clue.text: Use deception to get university place

parts.note: to lie is to deceive

explanation.surface: Someone cheats to get into university.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of', instead of.

clue.text: Soup Herod ordered with egg in it, for the group

parts.note: broth is a thin soup

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is egg-shaped

explanation.surface: King Herod asked for soup with an egg in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests Herod placed an order; it rearranges HEROD plus O into ERHOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood is a fraternity or association of people with a common aim.
